parts: Sweden, nineteen sixty-seven. A whole country changes sides of the road.
It is Sunday, September third, at ten minutes to five in the morning.
The cars, buses and trucks still on the road come to a stop.
Then the drivers cross to the other side.
So why would Sweden do this?
In nineteen fifty-five, Sweden held a vote on the change.
Parliament approved the switch anyway, in May nineteen sixty-three.
Drivers crossed over, and waited ten minutes.
At five o'clock, traffic moved off again, slowly, on the right.
That day, one hundred fifty-seven accidents were reported, and few were serious.
